daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR kept secret details of a newly approved Ombudsman replacement through a PAW (inter-term replacement) mechanism. Meanwhile, political parties continue positioning for future contests, with NasDem targeting a top-three finish in the 2029 election and party officials describing an increasingly competitive political landscape ahead. On the coalition side, Golkar stated that citizens have the right to form shadow cabinets, reflecting ongoing debates about political accountability structures.

  • PAN expelled the West Lombok regent who was caught in a KPK sting operation for corruption.
  • DPR deputy speaker Dasco responded to questions about the appointment of a new Jampidsus to replace Febrie.
  • The DPR questioned the involvement of the TNI in tax matters, raising oversight concerns about military roles in civilian administration.
  • The presidential palace addressed speculation about possible budget cuts for TNI and Polri.
  • A Constitutional Court hearing revealed "kitchen secrets" of MK judge Saldi Isra during a lawsuit over lecturer salaries.
  • NasDem youth wing leader Saan Mustofa urged the party's youth guard to stay clean, emphasizing integrity ahead of upcoming political battles.
  • President Prabowo and Vice President Gibran did not sit side-by-side during a cabinet session, with officials explaining the seating arrangement.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The DPR ratified defence cooperation bills with Turkey and Malaysia, formalizing bilateral security partnerships with both countries. Indonesia's Foreign Minister Sugiono attended an ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting where he stressed the importance of maintaining unity amid regional turbulence. On consular matters, Indonesian authorities dealt with multiple cases of citizens abroad: two Indonesians were held hostage in Myanmar with a ransom demand of Rp 200 million, while 1,203 WNI were repatriated from online scam centers in Myanmar.

  • The Director-General of Immigration confirmed that Indonesians who fled during a tour in South Korea will still receive state protection.
  • Indonesian police arrested a Palestinian national wanted by Interpol for a bombing case.
  • A police officer was killed in an alleged attack in Yahukimo, Papua, with authorities pursuing the perpetrators.
  • ASEAN urged the US and Iran to restrain escalation in their conflict.
  • Indonesia and Australia launched a healthcare transformation partnership to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the health sector.

Other

Indonesia is preparing to issue its debut US$1 billion Panda Bond on July 23, marking its first renminbi-denominated bond offering in China's domestic market. The government also announced that Indonesia has begun its first Russian oil imports under a 150-million-barrel procurement plan. On the energy front, the B50 biodiesel program is allowing Indonesia to cut oil imports by 750,000 barrels per day, significantly reducing dependency on foreign crude.

  • The rupiah strengthened as investor concerns over Indonesia's fiscal outlook began to ease.
  • Indonesia's new free trade agreement with the EAEU opens a US$3 trillion market for local products.
  • The KPK confirmed that Lebaran gift parcels for civil servants constitute gratification and fall under anti-corruption rules.
  • The KPK revealed that 29 land plots owned by the West Lombok regent were not included in his LHKPN asset disclosure, and the agency will pursue money laundering charges.
  • Indonesia plans to establish 40,000 fish farms to boost protein self-sufficiency across the archipelago.
